312:
(a) The entire area now embraced by the corporate limits of the city is hereby designated as a bird sanctuary.
(b) Adequate signs shall be erected and maintained at entrances to the city, within the discretion of the mayor and council, signifying the designation of the area within the corporate limits as a bird sanctuary.

314:
No owner or person in control of any animal or fowl shall permit that animal or fowl to run at large within the city. Any animal or fowl found at large may be impounded by any police officer or animal control officer and transported to the county pound where it shall be held or disposed of in accordance with regulations of the pound.
Cross reference— Authority to impound animals at large, Charter, section 38.
315:
No person shall keep or harbor any animal which, by loud or frequent barking, howling, yelping, growling, snorting or any other noise, causes serious annoyance to the neighborhood or people passing on the street.
Cross reference— Dogs generally, § 11-3-21 et seq.
316: It shall be unlawful for any person to have or keep any hog within the city, either on his own premises or on the premises of another, and whether kept in a pen or otherwise kept or confined on the property.
317:
(a) Diseased animals or fowl which might infect healthy animals or cause a menace to the public health, shall be isolated or destroyed and disposed of, as the mayor and council deem necessary.
(b) Any person who is the owner, or person having the charge of any animal or fowl, and knows that the animal or fowl has any contagious or infectious disease, or has been recently exposed thereto, and who sells, trades or disposes of such animal or fowl without first disclosing to the person to whom the same is sold, traded or disposed of, that such animal or fowl is so diseased, or has been exposed, or knowingly permits the animal or fowl to run a large, or knowing the animal or fowl to be diseased, knowingly allows the same to come into contact with any such animal or fowl of another person without his knowledge or permission, shall be punished as provided by section 1-1-8.
318:
(a) No person shall leave or deposit any poison or any substance containing poison in any street, lane or thoroughfare of any kind in the city.

324: It shall be unlawful for any person to keep, maintain or allow to be kept on the premises occupied by anyone in the city, or to allow to run or go at large, within the city any dog that is not protected by a current valid rabies inoculation administered by a duly licensed veterinarian, which vaccination shall be evidenced by a metal tag attached to a collar worn by the dog.
325: When a dog has bitten some person or is otherwise suspected of being rabid by the county health officer, it shall be quarantined upon written notice by the county health officer. The owner may board the dog in an approved veterinarian hospital. Should the owner fail to comply with such quarantine, the police shall immediately impound such dog and quarantine it at the expense of the owner. Such quarantined dogs shall be kept quarantined until released by the county health officer.
326:
(a) In the event any person is bitten by a dog within the limits of the city, it shall become the duty of such person or the owner of such dog when he has knowledge of the incident, to report such incident to the city police or county health department within 24 hours thereafter.
(b) It shall be the duty of every physician or other practitioner, to report to the police department the names and addresses of persons treated for bites inflicted by animals, together with such other information as will be helpful in rabies control.
(c) It shall be the duty of every licensed veterinarian to report to the city his diagnosis of any animal observed by him as a rabies suspect.

The dog control officer's authority to investigate shall include the power to enter on to public and private property for the purpose of periodic inspection.
332:

334:

335:
(a) Dangerous dogs and potentially dangerous dogs are subject to immediate confiscation pursuant to the grounds for confiscation in O.C.G.A. § 4-8-27.
(b) Dangerous dogs and potentially dangerous dogs that have been confiscated shall be taken to such impound facility as is designated by the contract between the city and Coweta County.
(c) Dog owners shall pay a confiscation fee of $15.00 and the daily boarding fee of $6.00 for each day the dog remains at the impound facility. Non-payment of either or both of these fees shall be an offense and shall be punishable under section 1-1-8 of this Code.
(d) Dangerous dogs and potentially dangerous dogs shall be returned to their owners pursuant to the provisions of O.C.G.A. § 4-8-27 and after all fees have been paid.
